en: An old sepia-tone postcard shows a street scene of a European city, featuring ornate late-19th-century buildings with pointed spires and elaborate fascias. To the left, there's a highly decorative historicist public building (likely the post office), and to the right, a simpler yet elegant urban residential/commercial building. In the foreground, a street sign reading 'Spark...' can be seen, likely referring to a 'Sparkasse' (savings bank). A few people are walking on the cobbled street. The sky is empty, and the view is down a quiet avenue. Printed text at the top says 'Döbeln. Königstraße mit Postamt.' and at the bottom '8727 Brück & Sohn Meissen.'
